system_description.narrative_title: Fragmenting Global Order: Power, Markets, and Technology in Tension
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, densely interconnected system driven by intensifying great-power competition (US-China, Russia-West), regionally proliferating conflicts (Ukraine, Middle East), and accelerating technological and financial disruptions. Monetary tightening and energy shocks are amplifying geopolitical stress while states weaponize trade, investment and emerging technologies (AI, space, rare earths) as strategic levers. Multilateral institutions and supply chains are strained, producing selective cooperation alongside tactical decoupling and securitization of formerly commercial domains.
system_description.scope: State actors, alliances and rivalries; international organisations; global markets (capital, commodities, bonds); strategic industries (energy, defence, semiconductors, AI); multinational firms and tech platforms; cross-border flows of goods, capital, data, and people; conflict zones and migration streams.

variables.name: Iran-led Gulf campaign and energy security
variables.description: Iran, Houthi proxies, Saudi Arabia and Western states are engaged in sustained maritime, missile and proxy attacks that are shifting control, risk and insurance costs across Gulf shipping lanes and global energy routes.

variables.name: Russia–West military and economic confrontation
variables.description: Russia and Western states (including NATO, the EU and the US) are escalating military strikes, sanctions, asset seizures and political measures that are altering security calculations in Europe and deepening systemic economic decoupling.

variables.name: US–China strategic economic and tech rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are intensifying competition over trade, investment, tariffs and critical supply chains, with summit diplomacy trying to manage tensions while each side pursues protective industrial and market measures.

variables.name: AI governance, safety and militarization
variables.description: Rapid advances in artificial intelligence by US, Chinese and European actors are reshaping technological dominance, enabling new military capabilities, surfacing safety incidents and provoking disputes over regulation and international norms.

variables.name: Global monetary tightening and capital shocks
variables.description: Major central banks (notably the US Fed, BoE and BoJ) are tightening policy and driving higher long-term yields, which is shifting capital flows, exposing debt vulnerabilities and amplifying macroeconomic stress across markets.
